{"body":"## When to use
Any task: implement one function from a prose spec, no tests given. Read the spec once, extract every concrete claim, then verify each claim by running code.

## Build the checklist
Before coding, write a short numbered checklist in your reply (not in a file). Pull items only from what the spec states:
- Signature/imports: keep them exactly; body only.
- Return type/shape: scalar, tuple order, DataFrame columns/index names, list element type, Axes vs Figure.
- Exceptions: only those named, raised exactly when the stated condition holds; check order if several could apply.
- Edge cases explicitly mentioned (empty input, single element, missing file, defaults).
- Formats shown in examples: exact strings, labels, rounding, NaN vs 0.
- Side effects: files, warnings, plots, subprocess behavior.
- Degenerate inputs: if inputs can be empty or zero-length, add an item for what to return then, and return a valid object of the stated type instead of letting a library raise.
- Input tolerance: if the spec describes data by role rather than exact label, add an item that the function finds it in a reasonable frame (e.g. any numeric column) rather than assuming one exact name.
- Concurrency/threads: if the function runs a loop, server, or thread, add an item that no unhandled exception escapes (guard dict/list lookups and removals; catch per-socket/per-item errors).

## Check it
Write a throwaway script (outside the repo or delete after) that imports the function and asserts each checklist item: type checks, `list(df.columns)`, `df.index.tolist()`, tuple unpacking, try/except for each named exception, and the documented edge inputs. For plots assert `isinstance(result, Axes)`; for files assert existence then clean up. Run it, fix failures, rerun. Also run any provided tests.

## Pitfalls
- Don't invent exceptions or messages the spec didn't name; don't swallow named ones.
- Match example output literally (labels, spacing, NaN).
- Respect stated ordering of tuple returns and list contents.
- Close files/plots; avoid leaving temp artifacts in the repo.
- Don't change signature, imports, or constants; don't edit tests.
- Don't assume a column name the spec never states; fall back to a numeric column.
- Don't let empty inputs crash inside a library; return the stated type.
- Don't let a background thread raise; wrap loop bodies in try/except and check membership before removing.","reason":"Trimmed wording to fit the 1700-char budget while keeping the added degenerate-input, input-tolerance, and concurrency items supported by the evidence."}
